title: Rose O'Neal Greenhow, letter written in cipher on mourning paper (Confederate spy ring, Washington)
correspondents: Rose O'Neal Greenhow → Thomas Jordan / Beauregard's headquarters (presumed)
shelfmark: NARA RG 59, Seized Correspondence of Rose O'Neal Greenhow (entry A1-986), NAID 1634036
folio_note: 4 images; one mourning-paper leaf in fragments, about 20 lines of symbol-and-digit cipher with clear words ('the', 'this') between cipher groups; second side very faint
status: Catalogue gives no decipherment. Greenhow's cipher (Jordan's symbol alphabet with code signs) has a surviving key, laminated, recovered from her effects (North Carolina State Archives, Greenhow Papers 1863-64), which the Rosenbach used to read her Beauregard note. Whether this leaf was read by Pinkerton's men in 1861 is not established. Key lead found in this sweep: NARA RG 45, M1091 Subject File of the Confederate States Navy, file 'DC - Codes and cryptography - Miscellaneous' (NAID 62017285, images 0483-0485) holds a 'Confederate cipher 1864' symbol table, docketed as found on Rose Greenhow's person when she drowned off Fort Fisher (Condor, 1864): symbol alphabet, digraph signs (th, ph, ch, sh, ee, ll, ss...) and code signs for Washington, Richmond, Lincoln, Pennsylvania Avenue, Virginia, South Carolina, regiment, infantry, cannon, soldiers; 'double letter, 2nd letter itself inverted'. The 1861 letters' signs (squares with dots/crosses, triangles, digits) look like the same family (viewed 27 Oct 2026).
why: Intelligence from the Washington ring before and after First Bull Run, in the original cipher; a readable test with an outside key.
score_note: Scored from the published description during the Oct 2026 US military/intelligence records sweep (research/nara_military/); not viewed
verify: Apply the 1864 key in NARA M1091 (NAID 62017285, images 0483-0485; also NC State Archives copy) to the scans; Get the NC State Archives key image (Rose O'Neal Greenhow Papers, digital.ncdcr.gov 378359); check Blackman, 'Wild Rose' (2005), and the Pinkerton report in the same series for a period decipherment
prior_art: open as far as found (checked 27 Oct 2026: NARA catalogue, Rosenbach blog, web); period decipherment possible, not located
